answer: The warrant is allotted on 1 January 2024. The tenure of warrants shall not exceed eighteen months from the date of allotment, so the last permissible day to pay the warrant exercise price is 1 July 2025 (18 months from 1 January 2024). The warrant holder must exercise the option to acquire equity shares within three months from the date of payment of the warrant exercise price. Three months from 1 July 2025 is 1 October 2025. Therefore, the latest calendar date on which the warrant holder can exercise the option is 1 October 2025.

citations.quote: The tenure of warrants issued in an initial public offer shall not exceed eighteen months from the date of their allotment. The warrant holder shall exercise the option to acquire equity shares against each warrant within three months from the date of payment of warrant exercise price.

answer: Yes. One passage identifies exceptional and/or extra-ordinary profits and income as ineligible for dividend payment, while the other identifies net unrealised gains arising on fair valuation of Level 3 financial instruments (including derivatives) as ineligible for dividend payment.

citations.quote:
Passage A:
Any exceptional and / or extra-ordinary profits / income shall not be available for payment of dividend.

Passage B:
A bank shall not pay dividend out of net unrealised gains arising on fair valuation of Level 3 financial instruments (including derivatives).

answer: Yes, the April 16 transaction is permissible. Under Regulation 15(7), an investment adviser cannot enter into a transaction on its own account contrary to its advice for 15 days from the day of such advice. However, the proviso allows the adviser to do so if it believes the situation has changed and it gives a revised assessment to the client at least 24 hours in advance of the transaction. Here, the revised assessment was issued on April 14, which is 48 hours before the April 16 transaction, satisfying the 24-hour advance requirement.

citations.quote: Provided that during the period of such fifteen days, if the investment adviser is of the opinion that the situation has changed, then it may enter into such a transaction on its own account after giving such revised assessment to the client at least 24 hours in advance of entering into such transaction.

answer: The maximum shareholding percentage a single entity (individually or together with persons acting in concert) can hold in a recognised stock exchange without prior written approval of the Board is five per cent (5%) of the paid-up equity share capital. However, this limit is fifteen per cent (15%) in the case of stock exchanges, depositories, banking companies, insurance companies, and public financial institutions.

citations.quote: A recognised stock exchange shall not be eligible for recognition if any person, individually or together with persons acting in concert with such person, acquires or holds or controls more than five per cent of the paid-up equity share capital of the recognised stock exchange, unless the prior written approval of the Board has been obtained. Provided that the limit of five per cent shall be fifteen per cent in the case of stock exchanges, depositories, banking companies, insurance companies, and public financial institutions.

answer: A mutual fund must pay its annual service fee before 15th April each year. The Board (SEBI) may, on being satisfied with the reasons for delay, permit the mutual fund to pay at any time before the expiry of two months from the commencement of the financial year to which the fee relates (i.e., until 1 June).

citations.quote: A mutual fund shall pay before the 15th April each year a service fee as specified in the Second Schedule for every financial year from the year following the year of registration: Provided that the Board may, on being satisfied with the reasons for the delay permit the mutual fund to pay the service fee at any time before the expiry of two months from the commencement of the financial year to which such fee relates.

citations.quote: Section A of the Directions on implementation of Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) shall come into force with immediate effect. Section B of the Directions on implementation of Unique Transaction Identifier (UTI) shall come into effect from January 01, 2027.

answer: The regulations require the issuer to give twenty-one days' notice of the proposed roll-over to the holders. If the notice is dispatched on 5 May 2025, the earliest date on which the roll-over can take effect is 26 May 2025.

citations.quote: it shall do so only upon passing of a special resolution to that effect and give twenty one days' notice of the proposed roll over to the holders of municipal debt securities

answer: The maximum time gap between any two consecutive board meetings is 120 days. If the first board meeting is held on 1 April, the second board meeting must be held by 30 July.

citations.quote: The maximum time gap of one hundred and twenty days between any two consecutive board meetings shall apply to listed entities.

answer: No. The original definition required each investor to invest not less than seventy crore rupees, while the November 2025-amended definition lowered the threshold to not less than twenty-five crore rupees.

citations.quote:
Passage A:
Regulation 2(1)(pa) (before November 2025 amendment): 'large value fund for accredited investors' means an Alternative Investment Fund or scheme of an Alternative Investment Fund in which each investor (other than the Manager, Sponsor, employees or directors of the Alternative Investment Fund or employees or directors of the Manager) is an accredited investor and invests not less than seventy crore rupees.

Passage B:
Regulation 2(1)(pa) (as amended w.e.f. 19-11-2025): 'large value fund for accredited investors' means an Alternative Investment Fund or scheme of an Alternative Investment Fund in which each investor (other than the Manager, Sponsor, employees or directors of the Alternative Investment Fund or employees or directors of the Manager) is an accredited investor and invests not less than twenty-five crore rupees.

answer: SEBI must dispose of the application by 24 April. The deadline is thirty days from the later of the receipt of the application (1 March) or the furnishing of all information called for (25 March). Since 25 March is later, the thirty-day period runs from that date, ending on 24 April.

citations.quote: The Board shall dispose of the application for grant of approval as soon as possible but not later than thirty days after receipt of application by the Board or, after all the information called for under regulation 12 has been furnished, whichever is later.
